name: aalib
why: Renders graphics as ASCII art via a portable library, a classic image-to-text transform with some charm.

brief.what_it_is: AA-lib is a portable ASCII art graphics library. It takes graphics drawing calls through a standard API and renders them as text characters, so programs can produce images on any terminal. The homepage describes it as a library that works on a terminal of any kind. The Homebrew package installs five executables built on it: aafire, aainfo, aalib-config, aasavefont and aatest.
brief.why_it_exists: The author's framing is simplicity: video cards, low-frequency monitors and crashing graphical apps cause many problems, and AA-lib is offered as the answer. The homepage says it gives old hardware more power.
brief.install_notes: The homepage gives no installation steps beyond the package. The download page (dated 2001) lists release candidate sources of version 1.4, plus a separate VGA library and text library that the DOS port requires, and an OS/2 patch. The Homebrew formula's executables are aafire, aainfo, aalib-config, aasavefont and aatest.
brief.standout: It is a 1990s-era text-mode rendering library whose origin story is a Linux penguin logo shown on Hercules monitors, converted to ASCII with a font-bitmap approximation table. The same author later made XaoS, a fractal zoomer, and the BB demo to show off the library.
brief.status: quiet. The newest news item is dated Apr 25 2001 (version 1.4rc4). The homepage says the project is moving from its original home to SourceForge and points to SourceForge news, which I did not fetch. I found no release or commit data for a recent version.
brief.caveats: The README is thin and the site is old. The online documentation and tuning pages were named but I found no URLs for them, so I did not follow them. Only release candidates from 2001 appear on the download page, and I could not confirm a current stable release. The site has a copyright notice from 1997 but I found no license text, so I cannot state the license. The Homebrew formula's caveats were empty.
quotes: AAlib is an portable ascii art GFX library.
It works on a terminal of any kind, it is fast and portable, it gives to you standard API.
